Photoreal studio render, ultra high resolution, wide 16:10 frame.

Subject: Olympus Mons rendered as one colossal mass of white Carrara marble.
Follow the true silhouette of the Martian shield volcano, not a pointed
mountain: an extremely wide, very low profile, flanks rising at a shallow angle
of only a few degrees, a broad flat summit plateau, and a wide shallow caldera
depression cut into that plateau near the top centre. At the base, on both left
and right, the shield ends in an abrupt vertical basal escarpment, a sheer cliff
wall dropping straight to the floor.

The mass spans the entire width of the frame and beyond, its summit reaching
only about half the frame height. Proportion matters more than detail: it must
read as broad and flat, wider than it is tall by a factor of at least four.

Material: white Carrara marble with fine cool-grey veining, denser in the
shadowed folds of the flanks and along the escarpment face. The surface carries
the long shallow ridges and radial flow ripples of a shield volcano, carved as
if by hand into stone.

Ground: a mirror-polished marble floor holding a faint blurred reflection of the
shield, dissolving into pure black before the bottom edge.

Light: a single hard key light from the upper left, low and raking, grazing the
shallow flanks so the ridges read; a weak fill from the right keeps the shadow
side legible.

Background: absolute true black, value zero, completely empty. No sky, no stars,
no horizon, no clouds, no gradient, no vignette, no fog, no atmosphere.

Nothing else exists in this image: no text, no logo, no glass capsule, no
waveform, no figures, no columns, no props, no scale markers, no snow, no ice.

Colour: strict greyscale, zero saturation, no colour cast. Wide tonal range,
brilliant near-white on the lit plateau, deep true black in the void, rich mid
greys in the veining. Very high microcontrast so the stone stays legible when
shown at twenty percent opacity behind an interface.

Sharpness: extremely crisp across the whole frame, no depth-of-field blur, no
grain, no noise, no chromatic aberration, no lens flare.
